title: On Sleeplessness
author: Physician Hesper Coldridge
pages: Every night a body does not sleep, it keeps a dream it did not spend. Three nights of this and the dream grows heavy. More than three and it grows wings. That is where night-mares come from.
They hunt the one who made them. They are pale, they shriek, and they come at the sleepless from above. A town where many do not sleep will have many of them. Close the shutters. Go to bed.
In the Sleepless Plague whole cities could not sleep, and the sky was white with mares. That is why the old law says the curfew bell means bed, and why your grandmother sang you down so firmly.
Remedies: warm milk and honey. A burrowfolk lullaby. A hearth-charm under the pillow. No dawnbrew after noon. If a whole village dreams of the same door, send for a Flamekeeper at once.
